title: Readiness Engine v2 — Implementation Specification
purpose: Defines the executable readiness engine that consumes pre-flight scan artifacts, computes per-item readiness classifications, enforces board visibility rules, generates readiness scores, and produces the session-level readiness report. This engine is the gatekeeper between the scan pipeline and certification boards.

exports.classifyReadiness(item, gateResults): Returns readiness classification: READY | MINOR_FIX | REMEDIATE | BLOCKED
exports.isBoardVisible(item, boardType): Returns boolean — determines if item appears in board queue
exports.getSessionPlan(items, readinessClassific: Returns prioritized work plan for the session
exports.verifyReadinessGate(readinessReport, gov: Returns gate pass/fail for phase authorization

readiness_classification_algorithm.description: Deterministic classification based on gate results. Runs after all gates complete. Classification order matters — first BLOCKED condition that matches wins.
readiness_classification_algorithm.pseudocode: function classifyReadiness(item, gateResults) { if (gateResults.gateNeg1.verdict === 'IDENTITY_BLOCKED') return { class: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'IDENTITY_FAILURE', score: 0 }; if (gateResults.gate0.verdict === 'FAIL') return { class: 'BLOCKED', reason: 'JSON_INTEGRITY_FAILURE', score: 0 }; if (gateResults.gate1.verdict === 'HARD_FAIL') return { class: 'REMEDIATE', reason: 'STRUCTURAL_DEFECT', blockingDefects: gateResults.gate1.hardFailDefects }; if (gateResults.gate3.verdict === 'HARD_FAIL') return { class: 'REMEDIATE', reason: 'IDENTITY_RECONCILIATION_FAILURE' }; const hasSoftFail = gateResults.gate2.verdict === 'SOFT_FAIL' || gateResults.gate4.verdict === 'SOFT_FAIL'; const hasWarn = gateResults.gate2.warnCount > 0 || gateResults.gate4.warnCount > 0; if (hasSoftFail) return { class: 'MINOR_FIX', reasons: gateResults.softFailReasons }; if (hasWarn) return { class: 'READY', warnings: gateResults.warnings }; return { class: 'READY', warnings: [] }; }

edge_cases.gate_1_hard_fail_on_certified: If a Certified item fails Gate 1 → REMEDIATE with severity escalated to CRITICAL. The item is in the learner pool with structural defects. Immediate remediation required. Flag in governance report as LEARNER_POOL_EXPOSURE.
edge_cases.gate_4_dl030_on_certified: If a Certified item fails Gate 4 with DL-030 CONFIRMED → REMEDIATE with severity CRITICAL. Wrong answer key in learner pool. This auto-triggers an emergency governance event.
edge_cases.all_gates_pass_but_unprocessed: Item with no defects and question_state 'Unprocessed' → READY for certification. This is the ideal pipeline state.
edge_cases.all_gates_pass_but_certified: Item already Certified with no new defects → READY_DELTA. No review needed unless content_hash change detected.

readiness_score_algorithm.description: Per-item 0-100 numeric score computed from gate results. Used for session prioritization — highest-scoring items processed first. Zero score = auto-blocked from certification.

deductions.condition: DL-026 present (any empty non-CC EW slot)
DL-021 present (any absent non-CC EW field)
DL-016 SEVERE (EW text describes wrong topic)

tier_mapping.70-89: YELLOW — Ready with warnings; minor fixes recommended

board_visibility_rules.description: Determines which items appear in which board's review queue. REMEDIATE and BLOCKED items are invisible to Quality and Certification boards — they cannot be reviewed or certified. This is the mechanism that eliminates the 89.5% readiness failure rate.

quality_board.display_as: READY items show with full detail. MINOR_FIX items show with warning badges listing the specific SOFT_FAIL reasons.

certification_board.display_as: READY items show with CERTIFIABLE flag. MINOR_FIX items show with DEFERRED flag — can be certified but warnings must be acknowledged.

governance_board.display_as: Full inventory visibility. REMEDIATE items shown with defect severity. BLOCKED items shown with block reason.

registry_board.display_as: Full inventory. Registry tracks all items regardless of readiness.

session_plan_generation.description: Generates a prioritized work plan for the session based on readiness classifications. Items are sorted by priority score — highest urgency first.

priority_rules.label: P0 — learner pool exposure, structural defect
P0 — wrong answer key in learner pool
P1 — learner pool exposure, missing distractor explanation
P2 — blocking certification, empty distractor slot

phase_gate_verification.description: Verifies that readiness metrics meet Framework v2 phase authorization thresholds. Uses the BF (Board F) metrics defined in SESSION203_THROUGHPUT_VALIDATION.json.

mid_session_drift_check.description: At session Tmid (~30 minutes), the Readiness Engine re-checks readiness classifications against current pack-file state. If any item's classification changed (e.g., DL-008 appeared on a previously-clean item), the pipeline halts for reconciliation.
checks: Re-run Gate 1 structural scans → compare to T0 artifacts
If any item's EW_Pattern changed → flag DRIFT_DETECTED
If any item's question_state changed without corresponding REVISION_HISTORY.md entry → flag UNAUTHORIZED_STATE_CHANGE
If any item gained a HARD_BLOCK defect → escalate — possible concurrent-write overwrite (DL-019 pattern)
mid_session_drift_check.on_drift: HALT all write agents. Spawn governance agent. Run G1-G5 reconciliation (per Session 31 runbook). Resolve before proceeding.

implementation_notes.stateless: Readiness Engine is stateless — it consumes scan artifacts and produces classification. No internal state between invocations.
implementation_notes.cache_strategy: Scan artifacts are read once and cached in memory for the session. Readiness classifications are recomputed on any artifact change.
implementation_notes.governance_hooks: The session plan output is consumed by Governance Board. The readiness report is consumed by Certification Board. Phase gate verification results are consumed by the session arbiter.
